titleEn: Is new irrigation tech worth a look?
titleZh: 新型灌溉技术值得关注吗？
summaryZh: 本文由《内布拉斯加农民报》资深编辑撰写，探讨了中心支轴式灌溉系统的新技术发展。文章指出，农民最关心的仍是爆胎、变速箱故障等实际问题，但制造商正聚焦远程诊断、实时故障报警等智能化平台。同时，中心支轴灌溉机被视为最早的田间自动驾驶车辆，未来有望搭载传感器和摄像头用于病虫害诊断。文章强调农民作为测试者和早期采用者的重要性，并呼吁关注新技术发展。
featuredReason: 本文虽聚焦大田灌溉，但其中关于远程诊断、实时故障报警、将现有农机作为自动驾驶平台搭载传感器用于病虫害检测的思路，对智慧畜牧行业的设备智能化、远程运维和多功能平台化发展具有直接的借鉴意义。

Is new irrigation tech worth a look?

Pivot Points: Convenience, peace of mind and ease are often driving the integration of new technology as much as return on investment.

Curt Arens,senior editor of Nebraska Farmer,Nebraska FarmerSeptember 18, 2026

schedule2 Min Read

Gearboxes and flat tires might be the biggest concerns for center-pivot irrigators, but new technology continues to evolve. Many ag technology startup companies, including those related to irrigation and water management, exhibited at this year’s Husker Harvest Ag Tech Pavilion at Husker Harvest Days at Grand Island, Neb. Curt Arens

We hear it all the time. Flat tires in the middle of the field during the growing season. Gearboxes failing. End guns that won’t shut off when they are supposed to.

These are the complaints irrigators have. If they are managing scores of pivots or systems, these issues become big problems during the irrigation season.

That’s why the center-pivot manufacturers have focused so much time on platforms that can offer real-time remote diagnostics. They are continuing to develop sprinkler systems that can alert farmers when and where there is a fault issue, such as tower misalignment, and what is causing it.

They can alert producers about pressure issues at the end of the pivot, or other water-flow problems that are occurring in real time.

The center pivot was one of the first autonomous vehicles working in the field. So, the same pivot companies continue to research ways to use that vehicle, while it is already working in the field, to do other things such as diagnose crop pests or diseases.

Related:Flags across Nebraska honor sacrifices of American veterans

Plenty of innovations

Twenty years ago, that kind of thing would have been thought impossible. But today, thanks to new sensors, cameras and capabilities, it is both possible and forthcoming.

At this year’s Husker Harvest Ag Tech Pavilion, numerous new ag tech startup companies showed off their stuff — their concepts, ideas, inventions and innovations — to farmers attending the show. The exchange and networking opportunities were provided by HHD and a partnership with The Combine,

Nebraska’s ag tech and food innovation incubator allowed farmers to gain new insights into what is next with crops, livestock and irrigation management. Those inventors and innovators also gained knowledge about what farmers and ranchers need.

That exchange of ideas is important, because many farmers today are beta testers and first adopters. That said, most producers are willing to wait it out, for the kinks to be adjusted in new platforms and inventions, before they try to integrate new technology into their operations.

They are more worried about the mundane things, such as end guns and pivot gearboxes, because these are what their concerns are today.

No matter which end of that spectrum you are on, it is important to stay up on new tech, because most assuredly, what is considered new technology today will be something we take for granted down the road.

Now, if only an innovator could come up with a pivot that fixes its own tires. That would be something everyone would be onboard with.

About the Author

Curt Arens

senior editor of Nebraska Farmer, Nebraska Farmer

Curt Arens began writing about Nebraska’s farm families when he was in high school. Before joining Farm Progress first as a field editor in 2010, and then as editor of Nebraska Farmer in 2021, he had worked as a freelance farm writer for 27 years for newspapers and farm magazines, including Nebraska Farmer. His real full-time career during this period was farming his family’s fourth-generation land near Crofton, Neb., where his family raised corn, soybeans, wheat, oats, alfalfa, cattle, hogs and Christmas trees.

Curt and his wife, Donna, have four children: Lauren, Taylor, Zachary and Benjamin. They are active in their church and St. Rose School in Crofton, where Donna teaches. The family now rents out their crop ground to a neighbor, but still lives on the same farm first operated by Curt's great-grandparents. The family runs a few cows and other assorted 4-H and FFA critters.

Previously, the 1986 University of Nebraska animal science graduate wrote a weekly rural life column, developed a farm radio program and wrote books about farm life. He received media honors from the Nebraska Forest Service, Center for Rural Affairs, Nebraska Association of County Extension Boards and Nebraska Association of Natural Resources Districts.

He wrote about the spiritual side of farming in his 2008 book, Down to Earth: Celebrating a Blessed Life on the Land, garnering a Catholic Press Association award.

translationZh:
我们总是听到这样的抱怨。生长季节，田地中央的轮胎爆了。变速箱故障。末端喷枪该关的时候关不上。

这些都是灌溉者面临的抱怨。如果他们管理着几十个支轴或系统，这些问题在灌溉季节就会变成大问题。

这就是为什么中心支轴制造商花了大量时间在能够提供实时远程诊断的平台上。他们正在继续开发喷灌系统，当出现故障问题时——比如塔架错位——能够提醒农民何时何地出了问题，以及原因是什么。

他们可以提醒生产者支轴末端的压力问题，或其他正在实时发生的水流问题。

中心支轴是田间最早工作的自动驾驶车辆之一。因此，同样的支轴公司继续研究如何利用这辆已经在田间工作的车辆来做其他事情，比如诊断作物病虫害。

**大量创新**

二十年前，这种事情会被认为是天方夜谭。但今天，得益于新的传感器、摄像头和能力，它既可能又即将实现。

在今年的Husker Harvest农业科技展馆上，众多新的农业科技初创公司向参加展会的农民展示了他们的东西——他们的概念、想法、发明和创新。交流和 networking 机会由HHD和The Combine合作提供，

内布拉斯加州的农业科技和食品创新孵化器让农民对作物、畜牧和灌溉管理的下一步有了新的见解。那些发明家和创新者也了解了农民和牧场主的需求。

这种思想交流很重要，因为今天许多农民是测试者和早期采用者。话虽如此，大多数生产者愿意等待，等新平台和发明中的问题被调整好，然后再尝试将新技术整合到他们的运营中。

他们更担心的是那些平凡的事情，比如末端喷枪和支轴变速箱，因为这些是他们今天的担忧。

无论你处于这个光谱的哪一端，跟上新技术都很重要，因为最肯定的是，今天被认为是新技术的东西，将来会成为我们理所当然的东西。

现在，要是能有创新者发明一种能自己修轮胎的支轴就好了。那样的话，每个人都会赞同。
